note: a question a verb invited, about an open case

71.desc: The bands have sworn to one shell now, and the shell has a king: Margery Pauw, the King of Thunes, on a barrel in a cellar under the Warrens. The Vendetta surges every week. Go in Disguise: with the ledger, to break it; with Wit, to parley; with Instinct and Coin, to be tried by its court and stay.

data.title: Fire at a Tenement in Imhoff Row

100.label: Unanswered: Fire at a Tenement in Imhoff Row
100.desc: The trail went cold. Bess Kempe walked. With the Rolls, this can be opened again in Study.

120.label: Burglary at Molenaar's Pawnshop
120.desc: Sebald Barker came down at prime to find the back shutter open and the strongbox empty. It was not a crocheteur's work, but it was not a nervous man's either. (Patricians' Hill)

134.label: The Inventory
134.desc: What the house says was taken does not match the guild's inventory. Someone knew what was worth carrying.

135.label: Prime Suspect: Bess Kempe
135.desc: Bess Kempe, a receiver from the Market. Drives a dray with a lame grey mule. (Accused in: Burglary at Molenaar's Pawnshop)

137.label: Partial: The Blade Read
137.desc: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. The blade was a chisel, chipped at one corner. Find the chisel, find the burglar.

142.label: The Hours
142.desc: The watchman cried two, and the dog was quiet. He cried three, and the shutter was open. One hour, and they knew the house.

145.label: Grey Hair on the Gatepost
145.desc: A rub of grey hair on the gatepost at a mule's height, and one hoofprint that lands wrong. Somebody backed a dray in here.

146.label: Margery Mercer
146.desc: Margery Mercer, the night porter. Wears great hobnailed boots, a soldier's. (Accused in: Burglary at Molenaar's Pawnshop)

150.label: Beadle de
150.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Steady: Working beside them, you do not tire.

153.label: The Getaway
153.desc: Wheel-ruts over the kerb, two people running, one of them limping under the weight. They did not care who saw.

154.label: Lijsbet Holzschuher
154.desc: Lijsbet Holzschuher, the owner's partner in trade. Owes a great deal to a moneylender in the Stews. (Accused in: Burglary at Molenaar's Pawnshop)

162.label: Protection in Sawyer Lane
162.desc: Stallholders have been paying for "protection" for months. Now Kit Schmidt's stall has had its awning slashed and its stock in the gutter for refusing. Nobody else will talk. (The Warrens) The Council wants it answered by the end of the week, and would take it kindly if Joan Fuller, of a Council family, were not the name.

165.label: Petty Thief: Ned Kessler
165.desc: Ned Kessler walked out of the Blood Court smiling. They are guilty, and now they are careful. Petty Thief, desrocheur. 1 crime on the record. Wears civet and rosewater, like a courtier. Has stood before the Blood Court once. Leaves less behind.

166.label: Partial: The Blood Read
166.desc: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. A great deal of it. The barber-surgeon in the Abbey Close stitched a hand the same morning.

169.label: Grey Hair on the Gatepost
169.desc: A rub of grey hair on the gatepost at a mule's height, and one hoofprint that lands wrong. Somebody backed a dray in here.

170.label: A Chit from the Pietersz Lane Lodging-house
170.desc: Folded small, in the wrong pocket. A chit from the Pietersz Lane Lodging-house, dated last week.

171.label: Joan Fuller
171.desc: Joan Fuller, a stallholder who pays. Never takes off a heavy gold signet. (Accused in: Protection in Sawyer Lane)

172.label: The Market
172.desc: Stalls, the weigh-house, pawnbrokers and cutpurses. The pillory stands in the square, and your Watch-house at its edge.

183.label: The Collector's Round
183.desc: Pencilled on the back of a broadsheet: market days, stall numbers, sums.

184.label: Dirck Mercer
184.desc: Dirck Mercer, a sergeant of the Watch. Smokes a clay pipe of cheap Dutch tobacco, one bowl after another. (Accused in: Protection in Sawyer Lane)

187.label: Petty Thief: Stoffel Claesz
187.desc: Stoffel Claesz, a rival in the trade. Walked from Fire at the Bader Print-shop. Petty Thief, espieur. 1 crime on the record. Wears great hobnailed boots, a soldier's.

188.label: Unanswered: Fire at the Bader Print-shop
188.desc: The trail went cold. Stoffel Claesz walked. With the Rolls, this can be opened again in Study.

190.label: Petition: The Hole
190.desc: A cell under the Watch-house with a table and one candle. Questioning is faster and draws out more Word. Costs 8 Coin.

192.label: Petition: The Rolls
192.desc: The court's old books, shelved and indexed. Unanswered cases can be opened again in Study. Costs 8 Coin.

193.label: Petition: The Thief-takers' Office
193.desc: A room let to men who know every fence in the city. Put a Case in Attend with 2 Coin and they get the goods back for a cut, without a trial. Some of what they bring back is a frame. Costs 6 Coin.

199.label: The Stews
199.desc: Taverns, bathhouses, dice-rooms and the spinning-house across the river. The people who own them own more than that.

201.label: Apothecary's Boy Vos
201.desc: Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted. Slot them into a verb to help. Thorough: Finds one more thing at every scene.

208.label: Clerk Tucher
208.desc: Reads a ledger like a romance and a forged hand like a confession. Ink under every nail. Slot them into a verb to help. Sharp: Reads raw proof properly even without the right instrument.

210.label: Fire at the Seiler Print-shop
210.desc: Somebody set fire to the Seiler Print-shop a day after the refusal. It started with a rag pushed under the door. The message came the next morning: the name of a tavern. (The Abbey Close)

212.label: The Warrens
212.desc: Tenements stacked against the wall, and cellars under the cellars. Everyone saw nothing, and everyone knows everything.

214.label: Motive: Bess Kempe
214.desc: The receiver had a buyer waiting for exactly what was taken.

ask.label: A locked door
ask.text: The back room is locked. Instinct finds the key under the sill; a watchman puts a shoulder to it. Left locked, whatever is behind it stays there.

story.title: Hands and Hours
story.text: What was left behind, and who could have been there to leave it. The marks narrow the door until only one person fits through it. It was Bess Kempe, a receiver from the Market. It has to be.

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book
journal.text: A pawnbroker keeps a book of everything that came through his door this week, and who brought it. Something from your case is in it. He would part with the page. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Week 16
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 2 Coin. Out there, the people who walked are talking about you. The broadsheet-sellers count the thieves abroad, and sing the number in the Market. Anselm Vogt has taken up one of your cases. The ledger: no case closed; 3 open; 6 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Rival Takes a Case
journal.text: Anselm Vogt is working Burglary at Molenaar's Pawnshop from the other side, with the Provost's watchmen. Answer it first, or they will.

journal.title: Hands and Hours
journal.text: What was left behind, and who could have been there to leave it. The marks narrow the door until only one person fits through it. It was Bess Kempe, a receiver from the Market. It has to be.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Joan de Witt walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: A Reason
journal.text: You let Bess Kempe talk about Sebald Barker. Their voice changes when they do. The receiver had a buyer waiting for exactly what was taken.

journal.title: New Ground: The Warrens
journal.text: Your feet take you somewhere new. Tenements stacked against the wall, and cellars under the cellars. Everyone saw nothing, and everyone knows everything. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.text: Somebody set fire to the Seiler Print-shop a day after the refusal. It started with a rag pushed under the door. The message came the next morning: the name of a tavern.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Sworn In

The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 7 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Wounded
journal.text: Someone was waiting on the stair of your lodging. You remember the first blow of the cudgel and not much after.

journal.title: A Scene Spoiled
journal.text: Somebody has been at Partial: The Blood Read before you could use it: moved, wiped, muddled. Anselm Vogt's people were seen in the lane.

journal.text: It arrives by carrier in a crate with the wrong name on it. It works perfectly.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and the Wit is back.

journal.title: Healed
journal.text: The barber-surgeon takes the stitches out. You can take a blow again. Probably.

journal.text: A moment on the bench, and the Wit is back.

journal.title: Promoted: Sworn Examiner
journal.text: They give you a new title under the city's seal, a better stipend and a heavier caseload. You are now Sworn Examiner. A magistrate will seal a Writ for you (an Accused with cause, in Explore), and the Council sends you more. The Council will send you up to 3 cases at once, and pay 2 a week. New petitions arrive with the letter.

journal.title: Answered by the Rival
journal.text: Anselm Vogt has closed Fire at the Bader Print-shop with a confession the Provost is pleased with. The Council notes who was quicker.

journal.title: The Trail Goes Cold
journal.text: Fire at the Bader Print-shop goes into a box in the basement. Somewhere in The Warrens, Stoffel Claesz hears the crier and laughs.

journal.title: The Rope: Bess Kempe
journal.text: Bess Kempe hangs on the Ravenstone before the whole city, and the ballad-sellers have the verses printed by nones. The crowd goes home satisfied. The Bishop's chaplain will remember that you were asked.

journal.title: The Council Takes Notice
journal.text: A letter, on heavy paper, under the city's seal: the Council will see you. Your attendance is expected.

journal.title: Guilty: Bess Kempe
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Bess Kempe is convicted of Hue and Cry: Bess Kempe, and the judge breaks his staff. Their name comes off the wall. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached.

journal.title: Condemned: Bess Kempe
journal.text: Bess Kempe goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, Banished, The Rope. The Council will follow your word, or its custom. Pleas arrive with the morning: The Bishop's Plea, A Family's Plea.

journal.title: The Market
journal.text: The stallholders know your face now. The Quarter is yours to walk: put it in Explore with Health for a round, or with a case to look for its people there.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at Sawyer Lane. You find: The Slashed Awning, Grey Hair on the Gatepost, A Chit from the Pietersz Lane Lodging-house. The first name on the board: Joan Fuller. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Commission from The Guilds: Protection in the Pietersz Arcade
journal.text: Stallholders around the Pietersz Arcade have been paying for "protection" on the first of the month, collected by a boy who takes the purses. Kathrin Kürschner refused, and lost their awning. Somewhere there is a receipt book. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name. The Guilds want the culprit shamed in the square or fined, and a brother of the guild not hanged.

journal.title: After the Burial
journal.text: You took the Council's letter the week after the burial. The man who did it walks the Hill in a good coat. Start with what is on the desk; it all leads to the same door in the end.

journal.title: A Commission from The Council: Burglary at the Molenaar House
journal.text: Endres Mercer is not sure when it happened: during the wedding downstairs. Only the cellar hatch was touched, and only the deeds and the coin taken. A neighbour reports seeing a tradesman's cart that no tradesman came from. Somebody knew the house. The Council wants it answered by the end of the week, and would take it kindly if Cicely Stromer, of a Council family, were not the name.

choice.title: The Pawnbroker's Book
choice.text: A pawnbroker keeps a book of everything that came through his door this week, and who brought it. Something from your case is in it. He would part with the page.

options.label: Buy the page
options.text: A page in a bad hand, with a name on it that you were going to have to find the hard way.
options.gain: A token that names a name

options.label: Threaten his licence
options.text: He gives you the page and a look. The Council's clerk hears how the Examiner does business.
options.gain: The token; the Council hears of it

options.label: Leave it
options.text: You do not deal with pawnbrokers. The word gets round that you do not.
